about: 2.49: extra paper accounts next to your main one (Mandeep, 10 Nov 2026, points 14 and 15). Each has its own money and its own trades (saved as source '<feed>#<id>', never mixed with the main account, the scorecard or the test bench). Paper only: nothing here can place a real order. 'pick' = which alerts the account takes; 'paper' = its account rules (same names as the main account's); capital null = the same as your main capital. Change the numbers here; old trades keep the rules they were taken with. 2.56: 'exit_style' (a chart exit from lab/exits.py STYLES) gives an account its own exit for every trade; pick.same_as_main takes the main account's alert types and strength.

best.name: Best only
best.explain: Takes an alert only when everything agrees: it is a Focus alert, strength 3, the risk check says PASS, the signal score is 70 or more, and that alert type has a good live record (20+ graded, 55%+ worked, option up on average after an hour) or it comes from a Strategy Lab rule that passed the strict out-of-sample bar. Few trades by design.

target3.name: 3% a day
target3.short: Aims for +3% of the account a day, top alerts only
target3.explain: Starts from the capital you type, adds every day's result to the next day (compounding). Takes only top alerts (Focus, strength 3, risk PASS, score 75+), one trade at a time. When the day's profit (booked + open) reaches 3% of the morning's money, it closes everything and stops for the day; at -2% it does the same. Honest note: 3% every day compounds to about 1,600 times in a year; no strategy tested so far does that, so this account measures how often a day reaches +3%, not a promise.

trail.name: Trailing exit
trail.short: Same trades as the main account, trailing exit
trail.explain: Takes the same alerts as the main account (same types, strength, risk check, lots sized from its own money) and differs only in how it exits: stop 1.5 x the 5-minute ATR of the index or stock, then a stop that trails 2.5 x ATR behind the best price, no fixed target, out by the day's exit time. Why: on 15,370 graded alerts (2-9 Nov) this exit made +2.0% more on the option per trade than the +30% / -20% premium exit, better on 5 of 6 days. Your call (11 Nov): test it here first; if it keeps beating the main account, switching the main account is your decision.
